ideas.title: 7 Dark Psychology Secrets to Read Anyone Instantly
ideas.angle: The video reveals high-stakes micro-behavior cues, such as the 'feet direction' rule and 'blink rate' spikes, that expose a person's hidden intentions before they speak.

hook.en: Look at their feet. It tells you more than their words ever will.

ideas.reason: Body language analysis and 'dark psychology' terms are currently peaking on YouTube and TikTok, with high retention driven by the 'viewer-testing' aspect of checking these cues in their own lives.
sources: Paul Ekman Group - Micro Expressions Research
Joe Navarro - Former FBI Counterintelligence Agent on Body Language
The Definitive Book of Body Language by Allan and Barbara Pease

ideas.title: How to Use the 3-Second Silence Rule to Control Any Conversation
ideas.angle: It demonstrates how tactical silence triggers an 'information vacuum' in the human brain, forcing the other person to over-explain, reveal secrets, or concede power.

hook.en: Stop talking. This three-second gap forces anyone to tell you the truth.

ideas.reason: Social engineering and 'power dynamics' content is trending among younger demographics seeking a social edge, particularly the concept of 'high-status silence' seen in recent viral charisma breakdowns.
sources: Chris Voss - Never Split the Difference (Tactical Silence)
Robert Cialdini - Influence: The Psychology of Persuasion
Journal of Applied Psychology - Silence in Negotiation

ideas.title: The 10-Second Vision Test That Reveals How Your Brain Processes Fear
ideas.angle: An interactive experiment where viewers stare at a center point while shapes move in the periphery; the speed at which they react identifies their brain's 'threat-detection' profile.

hook.en: Stare at the center. What you see next reveals your hidden survival instinct.

ideas.reason: Interactive tests ('If you see this, you are...') have the highest VVSA (Viewed-vs-Swiped) because they turn the viewer into the subject of the video, creating a personal 'loop' they must finish to find the result.
sources: Nature Neuroscience - Amygdala and Peripheral Vision Processing
Journal of Vision - Rapid Detection of Threatening Stimuli
The Stroop Effect and Attentional Bias Research
